correctness.rationale: The cut adds no fractional vertices because product-simplex edges change the forbidden biclique score by at most one. An explicit positive combination of surviving vertices obeys every projection supporting-normal inequality, giving unique projections and the exact distance. The exposed simplex has a computed positive Gram determinant; strict residual-mixture convexity proves only deleted vertices are global farthest points. Independent beta order statistics yield the finite hypergeometric removed-volume formula. Gamma central limit theorems and delta method yield the sharp Gaussian threshold. Exact rational tests cover 3,136 excluded vertices in 441 configurations, all Gram determinants and shuffle identities; 100 numerical QPs independently confirm, without replacing the proof.

value.rationale: A canonical edit deletes a biclique of a bipartite graph; this theorem determines the exact complete worst-case Euclidean response, its contact simplices and intrinsic Euclidean volumes, and the relative bulk volume response for every block size. A sharp Gaussian phase separates near-zero from near-one relative volume loss while the metric gap remains asymptotically nonzero. That bulk-versus-extremal decoupling is a motivated structural result rather than an arbitrary slice or small numerical improvement.
